alt: McKinstry and Wang (1991) found patients rating photographs generally preferred formally dressed doctors, especially older patients; ratings of photographs may not match real meetings. McKinlay (1975) found women on a maternity ward understood many medical terms poorly although staff still used them; the message is to use plain language, but the sample was narrow.
caption: Formal dress reassures; jargon blocks understanding.

alt: Disclosure is a balance: too little information leaves the patient anxious and unable to choose, too much at once overwhelms them. Five steps for delivering bad news: a private setting, check what the patient knows, give manageable amounts, allow time for questions and agree next steps.
caption: Tell enough, in manageable amounts, then agree what happens next.

alt: Directing (doctor-centred) and sharing (patient-centred) styles are defined. Study card: 359 patients of one inner London GP were randomly allocated to a style; satisfaction was measured immediately (89 percent returned) and a week later (58 percent). Directing gave higher satisfaction on almost all measures, especially for physical problems and prescriptions.
caption: Patients were more satisfied with the directing style, especially for physical problems.

alt: A timeline from noticing a symptom to attending, split into appraisal delay (deciding the symptom means illness), illness delay (deciding to seek care) and utilisation delay (actually attending). Interviews gave detailed reasons but rely on memory.
caption: Delay builds up in three stages before a patient attends.

alt: A table compares Munchausen syndrome (feigning or inducing illness for attention and the sick role, motive internal) with malingering (faking or exaggerating for an external reward, deliberate). Essential features of Munchausen syndrome are repeated feigned illness, pathological lying and moving between hospitals; supporting features include medical knowledge, scars, evasiveness, self-discharge and few visitors.
caption: Same behaviour, different motive: the sick role or an external reward.

alt: Four rows, one mark each: state the model, then apply low perceived severity (just a cold), a barrier (busy at work) outweighing benefits, and the lack of a cue to action to explain why Mr Hassan delays seeing a doctor.
caption: One mark for the model, then one for each part applied to Mr Hassan.
